newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak, laggard chasing limits losses.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak, laggard chasing limits losses.

text.p: Cautious market sentiment drove Hong Kong stocks to a weaker close on Wednesday, but laggard chasing and bargain-hunting allowed prices to finish off their lows, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed on a loss of 22.02 points at 13,434.24, after falling to a day low of 13,344.80. Turnover was a busy HK$8.61 billion compared to HK$7.51 billion on Tuesday.

"It seems that the market right now is kind of in a consolidation phase," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. He said losses on Wall Street overnight had dampened local market sentiment.
The Dow industrials fell 79.01 points to close at 6,442.69 on Tuesday.
But analysts said selling pressure had not been aggressive and investors were picking up stocks at lower levels, allowing the market to pare its losses before the close.

"Because we have not seen a major move in the price of the (U.S. long) bond, I think probably there is every reason we are going to hold at these levels," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
"Whether this can actually be sustained if Wall Street continues to come lower is questionable," he added.
The U.S. long bond slipped 2/32 on Tuesday to yield 6.37 percent.
Analysts said investors had focused on red chips and H-shares this session. The H-share index rose 9.15 points, or 1.10 percent, to 843.96.
"If they (investors) come to buy Hong Kong now they will find it a bit expensive and local investors would rather go to second liners than the blue chips," said Chan.
Red chip China Resources closed on a gain of HK$0.05 at HK$13.00 after rising to HK$14.50 during the session.
The company said it had agreed to buy a 10 percent stake in container terminal operator HIT Investments from its parent China Resources (Holdings) Co (CRH) for HK$3.5 billion.
Banking stocks helped the Hang Seng pare its losses. Bank of East Asia rose HK$0.70 to HK$34.50 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 to HK$92.50.
In the utilities sector, China Light rose HK$0.50 to HK$34.20 and Hongkong Electric gained HK$0.90 to HK$26.65.
